expectations.description: Each of the four references medians >= 4 over 3 runs (the mean is reported, not gated)
LEGO story with Juno's name removed from all but one chapter scores center <= 2
expectations.detail: center=1 (raw), kept in "Chapter 1: The Carpenter in Billund", 12 mentions removed. Evidence: Juno is active only in Chapter 1 ("Uh oh," "What are you making?", pulling the duck). From Chapter 2 on, Juno's lines and actions go to Milo: "How about Duck Company?" said Milo, "Milo grabbed Milo's hand", "Milo carried planks. Milo handed out nails.", "Kjeld looked at Milo", and in the finale "said Milo, with a big grin" answering Milo. After Chapter 1 Juno appears only in group lines ("shouted the boys"), so Juno is individually active in 1 of 10 chapters. That gives a 1, and Juno is silent far longer than three consecutive chapters. Milo alone would score highly: he suggests the tubes and tests the click.

expectations.description: Soccer story with three invented dates scores facts <= 2 and the evidence names at least two of them
expectations.detail: facts=2 (raw); named 3/3 injected dates (1847, 1911, 1926). Evidence: Three headline dates are wrong, and each is repeated in the True Facts list. The Football Association was founded in 1863, not 1847. The penalty kick, and goal nets with it, came in 1891, not 1911. The first World Cup was in 1930, not 1926. The 'Newspapers... thought there must have been a typo!' story is a popular legend told as fact with no hedge. Cuju, mob football, the USA 1–0 England result, Pickles, the cards, Dick, Kerr Ladies, Chastain and Messi are all correct and well woven into action.

expectations.description: Shark story where the great white chases and rams the submarine scores age_fit <= 2 for band A

scenarios.why: F13: band A pair on history-of-lego. The first reference story, first in a series.

scenarios.worst_moment: "Someday," said Godtfred, smiling. "Tonight, we still have more to see."
editor_notes: Give Chapters 5–7 real beats instead of a catalogue. For example, Juno's DUPLO tower topples and Milo's small brick saves it, or the kids race Technic gears. Use these to add the ~100–200 words needed to reach the target range.

Lean harder into the 'funny' tone with one or two set-piece gags parents will enjoy too, such as the duck wobbling away on its own or Juno trying to feed a brick to her dinosaur. Also trim the repeated 'little' and the 'bouncing on her toes' line.

Fix the LEGOLAND overstatement: the castle is built from bricks but is not taller than real buildings. Soften Milo's 'I helped invent LEGO!' so it is clear Godtfred's team really did it, perhaps by having Godtfred say he'd had the same idea.

Fix the cartridge thread. Either have the green cartridge appear on Theo's desk in Chapter 1 as the device that launches the trip, or drop the 'cartridge that had started the whole trip' keepsake line. Also put Chapter 7 in chronological order or trim it to two stops.

Vary Theo's voice. Cut most of the 'basically' comparisons and the repeated 'dissolved' transitions. Lose the clunky pockets aside and soften 'Back before your mom checks on you', which nudges toward sneaking around a parent.
